difficultyReason: One-step conditional gap. Stimulus contains transparent premise-to-conclusion bridge missing a universal quantifier linking membership to action. Correct answer supplies the needed conditional: 'all committee members who receive notice must attend.'
stimulus: The bylaws state that anyone who receives notice of a meeting must attend. The secretary sent notice to all committee members. Therefore, all committee members must attend the meeting.
questionStem: The conclusion follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The secretary always sends notice to every person who should attend meetings.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All committee members received the notice sent by the secretary.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The bylaws are enforced more strictly for committee members than for other employees.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Anyone who fails to attend a meeting without an excuse violates the bylaws.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The meeting will not proceed unless all committee members are present.

explanations.correct: The argument requires that all committee members actually received notice. Only if all committee members received notice, combined with the rule that all who receive notice must attend, does it follow that all must attend. B supplies this necessary step.
explanations.A: Whether the secretary should have sent notice is irrelevant; the argument assumes notice was sent.
explanations.B: Correct. This bridges the gap between 'secretary sent notice' and 'all committee members must attend.'
explanations.C: Strictness of enforcement does not affect whether the rule applies to all committee members.
explanations.D: Violation of bylaws and the duty to attend are not the same issue here.
explanations.E: The conclusion is about obligation, not about the preconditions for the meeting to proceed.

difficultyReason: Elementary one-step gap. Stimulus contains a universal rule about doctors and a specific case; conclusion requires application of that rule. Missing link is the classification of the subject under the rule.
stimulus: All licensed physicians must complete continuing education credits each year. Dr. Sanchez is a licensed physician. Therefore, Dr. Sanchez must complete continuing education credits this year.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if assumed, enables the conclusion above to be properly drawn?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dr. Sanchez has not already completed the required credits for this year.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Continuing education credits are the same across all medical specialties.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Licensed physicians who fail to complete credits face penalties.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Dr. Sanchez's license is current and valid.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The number of credits required has not changed since last year.

explanations.correct: For the conclusion to follow, Dr. Sanchez must satisfy the condition 'licensed physician.' The stimulus says Sanchez is a licensed physician, but D confirms the license is current and valid — thereby closing the gap between the rule and its application.
explanations.A: Whether credits have already been completed does not affect the obligation to complete them.
explanations.B: Uniformity across specialties is not required for the rule to apply.
explanations.C: Consequences of non-compliance do not establish the obligation itself.
explanations.D: Correct. This confirms Dr. Sanchez falls under the rule.
explanations.E: Changes to the requirement do not affect the duty this year.

difficultyReason: Transparent one-step conditional. Premises assert a rule and an instance; conclusion applies the rule. The gap is whether the instance truly satisfies the rule's condition.
stimulus: Only products that undergo safety testing can be sold in this country. This medication has undergone safety testing. Therefore, this medication can be sold in this country.
questionStem: The conclusion follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Safety testing is more rigorous in this country than in other countries.

choices.label: B
choices.text: This medication has passed the safety tests administered by the regulatory agency.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No product that has undergone safety testing is harmful to consumers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Many other medications have already been approved for sale in this country.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The safety testing was conducted by an independent laboratory.

explanations.correct: The rule 'only products undergoing safety testing can be sold' means the medication must have undergone the tests. However, merely undergoing testing is insufficient if it fails. B supplies the assumption that the medication passed, thereby closing the gap between the rule and the conclusion.
explanations.A: Comparative rigor across countries is irrelevant to whether this medication meets the standard.
explanations.B: Correct. The medication must not only undergo but pass testing.
explanations.C: Even if tested, a medication could still be harmful; this is too weak.
explanations.D: Prior approvals do not establish the condition for this medication.
explanations.E: The identity of the testing body is not required by the logic of the argument.

difficultyReason: Simple one-step gap. Rule is stated universally; premise identifies an instance of the rule's antecedent; conclusion applies the consequent. Missing assumption is that the instance indeed instantiates the antecedent.
stimulus: All employees who sign the non-disclosure agreement are required to return company property before leaving. Marcus signed the non-disclosure agreement. Therefore, Marcus is required to return company property before leaving.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if assumed, enables the conclusion above to be properly drawn?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Marcus is currently in possession of company property.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The non-disclosure agreement is legally binding on all parties who sign it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No employee who has not signed the non-disclosure agreement is required to return company property.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Marcus signed the agreement before he received any company property.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Returning company property is the most important requirement placed on departing employees.

explanations.correct: The rule requires Marcus, as a signer, to return property. For this to follow logically, the agreement must be binding on him. B supplies this assumption, confirming that Marcus's signature creates the legal obligation.
explanations.A: The obligation applies regardless of current possession.
explanations.B: Correct. The agreement must be binding for it to create requirements.
explanations.C: This discusses who else might be required; it does not establish Marcus's obligation.
explanations.D: Timing of the signature relative to receiving property does not affect the obligation.
explanations.E: Relative importance does not establish the requirement.

difficultyReason: Elementary gap. A universal conditional and a specific instance are given; the conclusion applies the conditional. The gap is whether the instance satisfies the antecedent without exception.
stimulus: Every scholarship recipient must maintain a minimum 3.5 grade point average. Elena is a scholarship recipient. Therefore, Elena must maintain a minimum 3.5 grade point average.
questionStem: The conclusion drawn above follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Elena's current grade point average is below 3.5.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Scholarship recipients are enrolled at a competitive university.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Maintaining a 3.5 average requires significant academic effort.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No exceptions are made to the 3.5 minimum requirement for scholarship recipients.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most students who receive scholarships maintain a 3.5 average or higher.

explanations.correct: The stimulus states the rule and that Elena is a recipient. For it to follow that she must maintain the 3.5 average without exception, we must assume no exceptions exist. D provides this necessary assumption.
explanations.A: Whether Elena currently meets the standard does not establish the requirement itself.
explanations.B: The university's competitiveness is irrelevant to the specific requirement.
explanations.C: Difficulty in meeting the requirement does not affect whether it exists.
explanations.D: Correct. The argument requires that the stated rule applies uniformly.
explanations.E: What most students do does not establish what Elena must do.

difficultyReason: One-step conditional chain. The stimulus provides a rule and a fact; the conclusion requires applying the rule. The missing link is confirmation that the fact triggers the rule's antecedent without complication.
stimulus: Only documents that are stamped 'approved' can be filed in the official record. This contract has been stamped 'approved.' Therefore, this contract can be filed in the official record.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if assumed, enables the conclusion above to be properly drawn?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The approval stamp is difficult to counterfeit.

choices.label: B
choices.text: This contract was submitted by the department with the most experience in contract review.

choices.label: C
choices.text: There are no other conditions that would prevent this contract from being filed.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The approval stamp is more commonly used than other stamps in the filing office.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Contracts that are filed in the official record are legally binding.

explanations.correct: The rule states approval is necessary; the stimulus confirms the contract is approved. To conclude it can be filed, we must assume no other obstacles exist. C supplies this assumption.
explanations.A: Difficulty in counterfeiting does not affect whether the approval is valid.
explanations.B: The submitting department is irrelevant to whether the rule applies.
explanations.C: Correct. This closes the gap by ruling out other blocking conditions.
explanations.D: The frequency of stamp use does not establish the contract's eligibility.
explanations.E: The legal consequences of filing do not affect whether it is permitted.

difficultyReason: Straightforward one-step gap. Universal rule about a category; specific instance identified as member of category; conclusion applies the rule. The gap is whether the instance is truly a member without exception or override.
stimulus: All software sold by this vendor must be compatible with Windows 10. The spreadsheet program was sold by this vendor. Therefore, the spreadsheet program must be compatible with Windows 10.
questionStem: The conclusion follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Windows 10 is the most widely used operating system in the market.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No software sold by this vendor is also sold by competing vendors.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The vendor has not made exceptions to the Windows 10 compatibility requirement for any software.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The spreadsheet program is the most recently released software by this vendor.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Compatibility with Windows 10 ensures that software will function without errors.

explanations.correct: For the conclusion to follow, the universal rule must apply without exception to all software, including this spreadsheet program. C explicitly supplies this assumption.
explanations.A: Market share of Windows 10 does not establish the vendor's requirement.
explanations.B: Where else the software is sold is irrelevant to this vendor's requirement.
explanations.C: Correct. The rule must hold universally without exceptions.
explanations.D: Release timing does not affect whether the rule applies.
explanations.E: Whether compatibility ensures proper functioning is not required for the obligation.

difficultyReason: Simple one-step conditional. Rule states a requirement for a category; instance is identified as falling under that category; conclusion applies the requirement. Missing link is confirmation that no exemptions apply.
stimulus: All architects licensed in the state must carry professional liability insurance. Patricia is a licensed architect in the state. Therefore, Patricia must carry professional liability insurance.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if assumed, enables the conclusion above to be properly drawn?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Professional liability insurance is expensive but necessary for architects.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Patricia has already purchased professional liability insurance in the past.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The state enforces its insurance requirement more strictly than other states do.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Patricia's license has not been suspended or revoked.

choices.label: E
choices.text: No licensed architect in the state is exempt from the professional liability insurance requirement.

explanations.correct: The argument asserts a universal rule and identifies Patricia as a licensed architect. For the conclusion to follow, we must assume the rule applies to all such architects without exemption. E provides this assumption.
explanations.A: The cost or general necessity does not establish Patricia's specific obligation.
explanations.B: Past purchase does not establish a current obligation.
explanations.C: Enforcement severity in other states is irrelevant to this state's requirement.
explanations.D: Suspension or revocation would disqualify Patricia from being licensed, contradicting the premise.
explanations.E: Correct. This confirms the rule applies universally to all licensed architects.

difficultyReason: One-step gap with clear conditional structure. Stimulus provides a rule and confirms an instance meets the rule's antecedent; conclusion applies the consequent. Gap is whether the instance fully satisfies all conditions.
stimulus: Any painting accepted into the National Gallery must be at least 50 years old. This landscape is accepted into the National Gallery. Therefore, this landscape must be at least 50 years old.
questionStem: The conclusion drawn above follows logically if which one of the following is assumed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The landscape is more valuable than most other works in the National Gallery.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The National Gallery applies the age requirement to all paintings it accepts without exception.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The landscape was completed by a well-known artist.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No painting less than 50 years old can ever be displayed in any major museum.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The age of a painting is the primary factor in determining its acceptance into the National Gallery.

explanations.correct: The stimulus states the gallery's rule and that the landscape is accepted. For it to follow that the landscape is at least 50 years old, the rule must apply uniformly to all accepted paintings. B supplies this necessary assumption.
explanations.A: Relative value does not affect whether the age requirement applies.
explanations.B: Correct. The rule must hold universally without exception.
explanations.C: The artist's fame does not establish the landscape's age.
explanations.D: What other museums do is irrelevant to the National Gallery's requirement.
explanations.E: Even if age is not primary, it remains a requirement for acceptance.

difficultyReason: Elementary one-step conditional. A universal rule about a class and a specific member are given; the conclusion applies the rule to that member. The gap is whether the member truly qualifies without exception.
stimulus: No student who plagiarizes can graduate with honors. Jordan did not plagiarize. Therefore, Jordan can graduate with honors.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if assumed, enables the conclusion above to be properly drawn?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Graduating with honors is a common achievement at Jordan's university.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Plagiarism is the only disqualifying factor for graduating with honors.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Jordan's academic work has been thoroughly reviewed by the university.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Most students who do not plagiarize are able to graduate with honors.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Jordan's grades are high enough to meet the honors requirement.

explanations.correct: The stimulus states that plagiarism bars honors; Jordan did not plagiarize. For it to follow that Jordan can graduate with honors, plagiarism must be the only barrier. If other disqualifying factors exist, the conclusion does not follow. B provides this assumption.
explanations.A: Commonality of honors does not affect whether Jordan qualifies.
explanations.B: Correct. This ensures that avoiding plagiarism is sufficient for eligibility.
explanations.C: Review thoroughness does not establish Jordan's eligibility.
explanations.D: What most students achieve does not establish what Jordan can achieve.
explanations.E: While Jordan likely needs high grades, the argument concerns only the plagiarism rule.
